subject: Specifying exogenous experimental variables in lavaan (R): how to exclude intercorrelation between experimental variables

messages.author: dc67ad569127dc67
messages.subject: Specifying exogenous experimental variables in lavaan (R): how to exclude intercorrelation between experimental variables
parts:
Hello everybody,

 

I am using lavaan to analyze the results of an experiment which included 2 binary categorical predictors ('strategies' and 'evidence'), 3 endogenous dependent variables (benevolence, integrity and credibility) and two exogenous control variables (distrust and orientation), one of which, i.e. orientation, was measured using a single-item scale.

 

This is how I've defined my model in lavaan.

 

full_SEM <- '

# latent variable definitions

  benevolence =~ Q2_1 + Q2_2 + Q2_3

  integrity =~ Q3_1 + Q3_2 + Q3_4

  credibility =~ Q4_1 + Q4_2 + Q4_3

  distrust =~ Q5_1 + Q5_2 + Q5_3 + Q5_4

# regressions

  benevolence ~ strategies + evidence + distrust + orientation

  integrity ~ strategies + evidence + distrust + orientation

  credibility ~ benevolence + integrity + evidence + distrust + orientation

# variable correlations

  benevolence ~~ integrity

  distrust ~~ orientation

'

 

This is the function I used to fit the model.

SEM_model_fit <- sem(full_SEM, data = SEM_data, fixed.x = T)

 

I have two issues:

1. I used the argument 'fixed.x = T' because the model includes two experimental variables which should not be correlated with each other, given that they were randomly distributed among the participants. However, when I run the fitting command above, I get this error message:

 

Warning message:

In lavaan::lavaan(model = full_SEM, data = SEM_data, fixed.x = T,  :

  lavaan WARNING: syntax contains parameters involving exogenous covariates; switching to fixed.x = FALSE

 

It looks like the parameter 'fixed.x = T' is overridden. Does anybody know why this may be the case? Could this be caused by the single-item scale?

 

2. The results of the analysis include the estimates for the intercorrelations between the experimental variables, which should not actually be considered.

 

Covariances:

                   Estimate  Std.Err  z-value  P(>|z|)   Std.lv  Std.all

.benevolence ~~                                                       

   .integrity         0.820    0.099    8.268    0.000    0.696    0.696

  distrust ~~                                                          

    orientation      -0.271    0.080   -3.391    0.001   -0.311   -0.224

  strategies ~~                                                        

    evidence         -0.009    0.015   -0.637    0.524   -0.009   -0.037

   

How can I therefore exclude intercorrelation between experimental variables in lavaan?

 

Thanks so much in advance for your generous help!

 

Matteo Fuoli

(University of Birmningham)

messages.author: ad188126f9138663
messages.subject: Re: Specifying exogenous experimental variables in lavaan (R): how to exclude intercorrelation between experimental variables
parts:
Matteo,
  I think that I see the logic in what you did.  Removing a parameter from the model means different things in different contexts.  It can mean fixing the parameter to zero, which is what you wanted.  However, in the context of fixed.x, it means not attempting to model a portion of the data.  That is not what you were trying to do although it might still make sense for you.

  To fix a covariance to zero, use something like this in your model specification:

strategies ~~ 0*evidence

  Notice that the covariance estimated in your model is near zero and not statistically significantly different from zero.  Estimating a zero parameter will not introduce bias.  It just eats a degree of freedom.

  As an alternative, you could follow the fixed.x strategy.  This will not fix the values inside the model.  Instead, it removes the variances and inter-covariances between exogenous variables from the moments to which the model is fit.  The values are simply read off the data.  So, they cannot be fixed to zero.  However they do not count for or against the degrees of freedom.

  The problem with your attempt appears to the the covariance between distrust and orientation.  Both of these are exogenous variables.  So, if you want to used fixed.x, you should omit this line from your model specification.  When lavaan finds a parameter that is not part of the fixed.x model, it switches back to the full model to accommodate that parameter.

Keith

------------------------
Keith A. Markus
John Jay College of Criminal Justice, CUNY

messages.author: dc67ad569127dc67
messages.subject: Re: Specifying exogenous experimental variables in lavaan (R): how to exclude intercorrelation between experimental variables
parts:
Dear Keith,

Thank you so much for your extremely clear and helpful response! As you suggest, I think that the most sensible strategy in this case is to fix the covariance to 0 using the formula you indicated. I have done that and the error message disappears. However, some parameters in the output are now marked as 'NA', which does  not happen when the covariance between the experimental variables is not fixed to 0.

Loglikelihood and Information Criteria:
 Loglikelihood user model (H0)                   NA
 Loglikelihood unrestricted model (H1)           NA

Number of free parameters                        44
  Akaike (AIC)                                   NA
  Bayesian (BIC)                                 NA

Would you or anybody else be able to explain why that is the case?

Thanks again for the very helpful feedback!

All best,
Matteo

messages.subject: Re: Specifying exogenous experimental variables in lavaan (R): how to exclude intercorrelation between experimental variables
parts:
Dear Keith (and all),

Please ignore my previous message. I have managed to figure out what was causing the NAs: the categorical variables were not numeric. I recoded the levels as  dummy variables, which solved the problem.

Thanks again and best,
Matteo
